# Infantile Colic

**Authors:** J B. Banks, Audra S. Rouster, J Chee

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Infants typically experience abdominal discomfort as a manifestation of infantile colic, which is a benign condition occurring in the second or third week of their lives. Persistent and inconsolable crying episodes in an otherwise healthy and well-fed infant characterize infantile colic. This condition distresses and challenges caregivers, leading to 10% to 20% of pediatric provider visits during the first few weeks of their lives. The key features of infantile colic are periods of inconsolable crying, irritability, and screaming that last for 3 hours or more without an apparent cause. Infants with colic often show symptoms in the evening, displaying red-faced appearances, leg-drawing, and abdominal tension. Unfortunately, traditional soothing methods typically prove ineffective during this phase. Healthcare providers establish a clinical diagnosis of infantile colic through a history and physical examination after eliminating potential pathological causes. When the symptoms spontaneously resolve, they confirm the diagnosis.
